entries.value: reviewers manually searched sequential replay footage, making a 30–40-minute match take roughly 60–80 minutes to review. (PDF p. 4)

rq3_entries.value: the tool predicts preferred strategies, identifies discrepancies, estimates their downstream impact, and organizes historical playstyle and preference evidence. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "In the Front-end Visualization Phase, the system offers the following functionalities: (1) Predictions of the preferred professional strategy at any moment [DR4]; (2) Quick identification of strategic inconsistencies for all players [DR1]; (3) Quantitative analysis of the impact of these inconsistencies on gameplay [DR2]; and (4) Insights into team and player playstyles and historical preferences to trace the origins of these inconsistencies [DR3]." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: experts inspect feature contributions, original video, and historical performance, then explain, refine, or reject model predictions. (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "Experts then integrated feature contributions, original video data, and historical performance to refine or reject these predictions." (p. 17)

rq3_entries.value: reviewer_noted — the interface labels model outputs as preferred professional strategies despite acknowledged imprecision, so uncritical acceptance is a plausible risk even though observed experts sometimes rejected predictions.
no — the interface support remains available throughout use and does not withdraw as competence grows.
experts must interpret the model’s evidence, judge context, and accept, refine, or reject its proposed strategy; this responsibility does not decrease with experience. (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "Its “human-in-the-loop” design allows experts to focus on the review itself—explaining predicted actions and analyzing the effects of current behaviors—rather than merely processing black-box outputs, thus enhancing review quality." (p. 17)

rq3_entries.value: single_session (1) — the comparative task exposure was one 30-minute analysis period after orientation. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "They then had 30 minutes to complete the tasks (Table 5), which were validated in a pilot experiment." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: the system enables users to identify strategy inconsistencies, understand their causes, assess game-outcome impacts, and ultimately enhance esports team collaboration. (PDF p. 18)
quotes: "The findings reveal that the StratIncon Detector enables users to identify inconsistencies, understand their causes, and assess their impacts on game outcomes, ultimately enhancing team collaboration in esports." (p. 18)

claim_entries.value: between_subject — participants were divided into separate system and baseline groups. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "To avoid order effects, we implemented a between-subjects design, dividing the 24 participants—22 males and 2 females—into two groups of 12." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: 24 — the comparative user study involved 24 participants. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "We recruited 24 participants (22 males, 2 females), aged 18 to 28 years (mean = 21.46, SD = 2.43)." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: domain_students — players, coaches, and analysts came from local university esports teams. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Given the system’s complexity, participants were selected for their deep understanding of relevant games and competitive events, including players, coaches, and analysts from local university teams." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: baseline_system — the comparison group used scoregg and LOL Esports. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Group A used our system, StratIncon Detector, while Group B analyzed the match using scoregg and LOL Esports, common tools for professional post-match analysis." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: test_only — the study reports Mann–Whitney U tests and p-values without effect sizes. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Since the samples from all participants did not adhere to a normal distribution, and considering the relatively small sample size in our experiment, we utilized the Mann-Whitney U Test [37]." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: 30-minute task period plus a 10-minute orientation — participants completed one bounded analysis session. (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Prior to the analysis, participants attended a 10-minute orientation session to familiarize themselves with the system’s content, data distribution, and operations, allowing for preliminary trials." (p. 15)
"They then had 30 minutes to complete the tasks (Table 5), which were validated in a pilot experiment." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: no significant differences were found for clarity, simplicity, or intelligibility. (PDF p. 16)
quotes: "Despite the StratIncon Detector performing better, the difference was not significant (H2c rejected, 𝑝 = 0.128)." (p. 16)

"The simplicity score of the baseline system (Mean = 5.667, SD = 1.614, Median = 6) was slightly higher than that of the StratIncon Detector (Mean = 5, SD = 1.044, Median = 5), but the difference was not significant (H3a rejected, 𝑝 = 0.129)." (p. 16)

"Additionally, participants found both systems easy to understand, resulting in high intelligibility scores for the proposed system (Mean = 6.083, SD = 0.515, Median = 6) and the baseline system (Mean = 5.583, SD = 0.996, Median = 6), with no significant difference between them (H3b rejected, 𝑝 = 0.173)." (p. 16)

claim_entries.value: short, one-session self-report comparisons support improved analysis experience, but not the broader conclusion that the tool ultimately enhances real esports teamwork. (PDF pp. 15, 18)
quotes: "They then had 30 minutes to complete the tasks (Table 5), which were validated in a pilot experiment." (p. 15)

"The findings reveal that the StratIncon Detector enables users to identify inconsistencies, understand their causes, and assess their impacts on game outcomes, ultimately enhancing team collaboration in esports." (p. 18)

paper_code_entries.value: professional MOBA esports post-match strategy analysis — the system supports professional teams’ review of strategic discrepancies and their gameplay consequences. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Based on insights from our observational study with experts, we developed the interactive visual analytics system StratIncon Detector to help professional teams identify strategic inconsistencies and evaluate their impact on gameplay, as illustrated in Figure 1." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support is designed for current post-match interpretation and future strategic planning, not a measured learning intervention. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Based on insights from our observational study with experts, we developed the interactive visual analytics system StratIncon Detector to help professional teams identify strategic inconsistencies and evaluate their impact on gameplay, as illustrated in Figure 1." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: expert_or_professional — the intended users are professional players and coaches. (PDF p. 1)
quotes: "To tackle these challenges, we present the StratIncon Detector, a visual analytics system designed to assist professional players and coaches in efficiently identifying strategic inconsistencies." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: evaluation_or_judgment_gap — existing replay review could not efficiently identify, explain, or quantify strategic inconsistencies and their later effects. (PDF p. 4)
quotes: "When using the official replay system to identify inconsistencies, players often struggle to quantify the impact and severity of these issues on subsequent game developments, relying heavily on personal experiences." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the comparative study measured participants’ ratings of how well the tools supported analysis tasks. (PDF p. 16)
quotes: "We performed Mann-Whitney U Test to assess the difference in the participants’ ratings and the results are shown in Table 6 and Figure 11." (p. 16)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — the paper also benchmarks recognition, classification, and prediction components. (PDF p. 9)
quotes: "Performance metrics for DETR, Swin-Transformer, and LSTM are detailed in Table 3, with experimental specifics in Table 4." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — four coordinated views organize review from overview and event selection to evidence and historical detail. (PDF p. 9)
quotes: "Iteratively refined through expert feedback, the system includes four views: the Replay View, the Player Inconsistency View, the Team Performance View, and the Player Preference View." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the discrepancy display makes conflicts between observed and preferred strategy explicit. (PDF p. 11)
quotes: "The inconsistency glyph appears only when there is a discrepancy between real-time and preferred professional strategies." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — selecting a different event immediately recalculates the displayed impact of each discrepancy for that event. (PDF p. 11)
quotes: "Furthermore, selecting a different event icon on the timeline dynamically updates the glyph sizes to show their impact on the new event." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — strategy predictions are generated from the immediately preceding match state rather than fixed content. (PDF p. 9)
quotes: "This model uses information from the previous five frames to forecast the next one." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — experts and the model divide the analysis, with experts retaining interpretation and judgment. (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "Its “human-in-the-loop” design allows experts to focus on the review itself—explaining predicted actions and analyzing the effects of current behaviors—rather than merely processing black-box outputs, thus enhancing review quality." (p. 17)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — DETR and Swin-Transformer recognize state and behavior, while an LSTM predicts the next-frame strategy representation. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "During the Back-end Engine Phase, we train a DETR model on manually annotated images to detect champion categories and local coordinates, while a Swin-Transformer recognizes behavioral categories." (p. 7)
"Additionally, we train an LSTM model to predict the strategy triadic model for the next frame based on the previous five frames." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the scaffold’s semantic content comes from conventional computer-vision and sequence models rather than an LLM. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "During the Back-end Engine Phase, we train a DETR model on manually annotated images to detect champion categories and local coordinates, while a Swin-Transformer recognizes behavioral categories." (p. 7)
"Additionally, we train an LSTM model to predict the strategy triadic model for the next frame based on the previous five frames." (p. 7)

limitations: "First, the training data comes from only 50 matches across six events, which does not adequately represent the diversity of teams and player styles." (PDF p. 18)
"While these matches yield over 100,000 frame images, simply increasing the match count would significantly heighten the training burden." (PDF p. 18)
"Moreover, match videos from the LOL Esports website exhibit frame-skipping phenomena, characterized by abrupt transitions or sparse frames." (PDF p. 18)

"Second, while ideal system evaluation would involve experts and participants replaying their matches for comparative analysis, our user study participants are drawn from various teams and roles to enhance statistical reliability." (PDF p. 18)

"Additionally, the collaborating experts lack prominence, and their match records are poorly documented, limiting the data available for robust model training and affecting statistical insights." (PDF p. 18)
"Third, the experts’ predefined behavior still lacks precision." (PDF p. 18)

"Lastly, experts also noted some additional potentially lower-ranked factors beyond the primary concerns in [KC1-KC3], such as skill cooldown durations, minion waves and hero positioning." (PDF p. 18)
"Furthermore, battlefield environmental factors such as bushes and vision mechanics should also be considered." (PDF p. 18)
"Expanding these considerations will require more comprehensive log data and map layout data, posing a challenge for future research." (PDF p. 18)
boundary_conditions: "In terms of generalizability, experts suggest that our system has strong potential for adaptation across different MOBA games, provided that data preprocessing is handled carefully." (PDF p. 18)
"When log data is unavailable, involving domain experts in defining behaviors could be beneficial." (PDF p. 18)

"Regarding scalability, the current implementation of the StratIncon Detector utilizes a dataset of approximately 100,000 frame images, with each match generating 40-50 inconsistency points—around 10 per player." (PDF p. 18)
cards.work_domain: professional MOBA esports post-match strategy analysis
cards.claim: the system enables users to identify strategy inconsistencies, understand their causes, assess game-outcome impacts, and ultimately enhance esports team collaboration
